nodes.source_text: Figure 2a reveals the initial discharge (protonation) capacity of 104 mAh/g with the first-cycle Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 77% where the galvanostatic charge/discharge (GCD) profiles are generally sloping. The theoretical capacity is 110 mAh/g if one proton/hydronium gets inserted per WO₃ formula unit

nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry with EQCM monitoring mass evolution
nodes.source_text: The first cathodic scan in cyclic voltammetry (CV) shows two reduction peaks at -0.1 and -0.45 V and two corresponding oxidation peaks at +0.08 and -0.23 V... EQCM monitored the electrode mass evolution during the initial 5 CV cycles... during protonation, ∼0.25 lattice H₂O was expelled first from WO₃·0.89H₂O along with ∼0.25 proton inserted simultaneously (0 to -0.25 V), and then ∼0.30 naked proton was incorporated (-0.25 to -0.40 V), followed by ∼0.17 H₃O⁺ inserted afterward (-0.40 to -0.55 V)

nodes.description: Rate capability testing from 1C to 100C (1C = 100 mA/g)
nodes.source_text: Figure 4a demonstrates deprotonation capacity values of ∼90, ∼75, ∼70, ∼60, ∼50, and ∼30 mAh/g at 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 C, respectively

nodes.description: Long-term cycling stability at 2 A/g for 20,000 cycles
nodes.source_text: At the current rate of 2 A/g, the charge capacity increases to above 80 mAh/g in the first 50 cycles, which is stable during the following 20 000 cycles... The CE is 87% for the first cycle followed by a rapid increase within the first 5 cycles, and stays at an average of 99%

nodes.source_text: The b-values of redox peaks demonstrate prominent pseudocapacitive behavior of H⁺ storage: 0.92, 0.90, 0.87, and 0.94 for R1, R2, O2, and O1 (Figure 4b)
the small charge-transfer resistance (R_CT) of less than 10 Ω and a low activation energy of 8.2 kJ/mol derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show the as-prepared tungsten oxide comprises nanofibers ~500 nm long and ~40 nm wide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared tungsten oxide comprises nanofibers, ~500 nm long and ~40 nm wide, as shown by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show nanofibers of the tungsten oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared tungsten oxide comprises nanofibers, ~500 nm long and ~40 nm wide, as shown by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images corroborate the refined crystallographic structure of WO₃·0.6H₂O nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The refined crystallographic structure is depicted in Figure 1b, and the Rietveld refinement results are summarized in Table S1, which are corroborated by the HRTEM images (Figure 1c,d and Figure S2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals the oxidation state of tungsten being W(VI) with the 4f_{5/2} and 4f_{7/2} binding energies at 35.7 and 36.8 eV, respectively. The absence of W(V) indicates a lack of cationic species within the WO₃ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveals the oxidation state of tungsten being W(VI) with the 4f_{5/2} and 4f_{7/2} binding energies at 35.7 and 36.8 eV, respectively (Figure S3a). The absence of W(V) indicates a lack of cationic species within the WO₃ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA reveals that there exists 0.6 H₂O per WO₃ formula unit based on the mass loss above 100°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analyses (TGA) reveal that there exists 0.6 H₂O per WO₃ formula unit based on the mass loss above 100°C (Figure S3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern presents a hexagonal structure (space group P6/mmm) with lattice parameters a = 7.35780 Å, b = 7.35780 Å, and c = 3.81746 Å after heating at 100°C. Rietveld refinement reveals tunnel structure with mobile zeolitic water molecules in dodecagon tunnels.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1a, the XRD pattern presents a hexagonal structure (space group P6/mmm) with lattice parameters of a = 7.35780 Å, b = 7.35780 Å, and c = 3.81746 Å. The Rietveld refinement analysis reveals two possible locations of zeolitic water molecules...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of WO₃·0.6H₂O is 32.74 m²/g with primarily macropores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We have measured the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area of WO₃·0.6H₂O, which is merely 32.74 m²/g, where the N₂ sorption isotherm and pore size distribution (PSD) are shown in Figure S5.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando EQCM reveals three-tier proton insertion process: first stage 0.25 H⁺ inserted with 0.25 lattice H₂O expelled, second stage 0.30 naked H⁺ inserted, third stage 0.17 H₃O⁺ inserted per formula unit.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the EQCM results during protonation... ~0.25 lattice H₂O was expelled first from WO₃·0.89H₂O along with ~0.25 proton inserted simultaneously (0 to -0.25 V), and then ~0.30 naked proton was incorporated (-0.25 to -0.40 V), followed by ~0.17 H₃O⁺ inserted afterward (-0.40 to -0.55 V).
